newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich re-election camp says speaker has big lead.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich re-election camp says speaker has big lead.

text.p: Newt Gingrich's re-election campaign Tuesday released a new opinion poll showing the House speaker 25 points ahead of Democratic challenger Michael Coles.
The survey, which put the Georgia Republican's likely margin of victory over Coles at 57-32 percent, was conducted by American Viewpoint on Oct. 23-24 and had a five percentage point margin of error.

The Alexandria, Virginia-based group said 400 likely voters from Georgia's 6th Congressional District gave the House Speaker a 60 percent favourability rating -- much higher than in national polls -- compared with 46 percent for Coles.
The poll came one week after a survey for ABC's Atlanta affiliate, WSB-TV, and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution gave Gingrich a lead of only 14 percentage points.

That survey also showed Coles running about even with Gingrich among women, a result viewed by some experts as evidence that the Republican's popularity was also being undercut by the "gender gap" seen elsewhere in the country.
Meanwhile the Coles campaign said it has conducted several polls showing a much closer race, but the Democrat has never released the results.
Earlier in the campaign the Gingrich camp published an opinion poll putting the Speaker's lead at 29 points.

An American Viewpoint memorandum, which was released by "Friends of Newt Gingrich," said the latest survey showed Gingrich led Coles 50-38 percent among women, including so-called "soccer moms" who have voiced strong support for Democrats in other parts of the country.
